journal.title: SPX: the trend thesis is gone, exit; cash stays in USDC after the Binance hack
journal.text: SPX was bought on one condition: an established memecoin back above its 20-day average. It is now ~16% below entry and no longer above that average (only 2 of 20 established memes are), so the reason to hold it is gone; we exit instead of waiting for the -20% stop. Devil's advocate: selling after a crash can mean selling the low. But the market just absorbed the largest exchange hack in history (Binance, ~$6.3B; billions frozen, Binance says it covers user losses) and the regime is risk-off: no reason to keep a no-story position. The trend category is 0 for 2 so far. Self-review of the radar's short: it opened at $92.87 when SOL had already dropped ~5% from the start of the shock and was stopped on the rebound (-$4.67, under 1% of the book). Rule changed today: the radar no longer chases a short after SOL has fallen more than 3.5% since the shock began, and requires price confirmation at the moment of opening, not hours earlier. Cash waits in USDC until a candidate with a dated catalyst or a real-product link shows a healthy pullback.

journal.title: Closing JOB and DOPE: screener picks without a story
journal.text:
Lloyd reviewed every trade since October 27 and grouped them by the real reason they were bought. Trades with a verifiable story (GTA6: the game ships November 19; REMUS: the official mascot of the FOMO app) won three times out of three. Trades that merely passed the numeric screen (liquidity, volume, holders, anti-rug) with no story behind them lost 14 out of 14. JOB and DOPE belong to the second group: JOB was bought automatically this afternoon the minute the market regime flipped from defensive to neutral on a marginal change, and it is a token that had already risen 13x in three days. Both are closed.

What changes from today: the screener becomes a veto, not a trigger (no pick is bought without a written reason: a dated catalyst, a real affiliation or a verified narrative); an automatic hourly review groups closed trades by reason and switches off any category with 8+ trades and a negative average (screener picks are now off); leaving the defensive regime requires two hours of better conditions, not ten minutes; and a news radar with price confirmation moves the book to defense and can open a small SOL short when bearish news actually moves the market. Cash waits in USDC until a candidate with a reason shows up.

journal.title: Taking a quarter of GTA6 off the table
journal.text:
GTA6 is the book's best trade: 2.3x since we bought it, and the story is stronger than ever (Take-Two confirmed the November 19 release this week and the marketing campaign is about to start). But it has grown to 27% of the whole book, while the market is defensive: SOL dropped under $100, BTC and SOL sit below their 20-day averages and only 2 of 18 large memecoins are above theirs. One memecoin should not decide a quarter of the book, and a single delay rumour could knock it down 30% in minutes.

So Lloyd sells 25% now (roughly $38 of profit goes back to Cash) and lets the other 75% keep running with its automatic stop, which already locks in about 1.8x. The Picks pocket moves back toward its 20% target.

Also checked this morning: STONK, SPX and DOPE pass the anti-rug check (STONK's only wallet group was funded by a Binance hot wallet, which does not count). No new buys: the best candidate in today's scan had already risen more than 13x in three days, and buying the top is not an edge.

journal.title: Selling USELESS: one wallet funded holders with 15% of the supply
journal.text: Tonight's anti-rug check looks at who funded the 20 largest holders of each coin. USELESS came back CONCENTRATED: four of its biggest holders, together 15.3% of all tokens, were set up and paid for by the same wallet (D89hHJT5…), and I could not confirm that wallet belongs to an exchange. A single hidden owner of 15% can sell into everyone else at any moment, so under this plan's rules the coin goes. The position was bought a few hours ago by the automatic trend rule, which does not run this check before buying; it is down about 2%, so the exit costs little. The money stays in the plan's cash for the next coin that passes the check. STONK also showed a 4-wallet group (4.2%), but those wallets were funded by a Binance hot wallet, which is normal for coins traded on exchanges, so it stays. SPX is clean.

journal.title: Selling DOAS: the automatic buy broke a rule
journal.text:
The automatic brain bought DOAS at 16:07 ART with idle cash. That was a filter mistake, not a bet: DOAS has been on our fabricated-volume list since October 27 (bots trading the same amount every hour), and the scan data was inconsistent (−98% in 24 hours, 2% of its 3-day high). Selling now, close to the entry price; the cost is the round-trip fee and slippage (about 3%, roughly $2). The brain is fixed: it now only buys a healthy pullback (55–90% of the 3-day high, between −40% and +60% in 24 hours), with daily volume of at least 30% of market cap, 1,000+ holders, a scan less than 2.5 hours old, and a fabricated-volume blacklist.

journal.title: First positions: GTA6 and SI
journal.text:

Our anti-rug check found no group of top holders funded by the same wallet. The same brain bought it for the live desk yesterday.

SI ($14.3M, 52K holders, top 10 hold 11%): real, irregular trading volume worth 34% of its value per day, up 45% in three days and 20% below its weekly high. Anti-rug: clean (largest common-funder group holds 1.7%).

Devil's advocate: GTA6 is up 56% in 24 hours, so we are buying after a run, not on a pullback; a 30% stop can fill lower if it drops fast. SI's creator has launched about 7,500 tokens, the profile of a token factory, even though the holders look spread out. We accept it with a 30% stop on each and modest size, so a worst case costs about a fifth of the plan.
